SCENE 04 — Tending existing embers — final edit6.600s (12.800–19.400s)
Setting and framing: Stable close-up from a gently elevated three-quarter angle. A charred bough and ember bed fill the middle half of the frame, with the contact point near x=58%, y=60%. One cropped anonymous human hand enters upper-right, gripping the far end of a single dry twig. Keep the twig tip, coals and supporting surfaces clear; background detail falls into broad cool earth shapes. Keep the lower fifth quiet.
Lighting: Cool diffuse shade over ash-gray soil and charcoal wood, with small ember-orange accents. Existing embers cast a weak local warm tint on the twig underside and nearby palm. The caught flame strengthens only the local warmth at the end.
First frame: One cropped human hand grips the far end of one short straight unbranched dry twig. Its single blunt tip hovers with a clear gap above a small red-orange glowing ember bed beside one charred bough and a few coal pieces. There are no visible flames, and no mascot or human face.
Action: Show one continuous tending action in this order: lower the single straight twig with a stable grip; establish secure support on the existing charred surfaces with its blunt tip against the embers; release it only after support is established; then withdraw the hand completely along one clear path toward the upper-right. After release the twig stays stationary. Begin with subdued ember glow and no visible flames. A small faceless flame catches only after placement at the twig–ember contact; keep its base anchored there. No extra hand, forked twig or tool.
Edit source: clips/edit-v2/04-tight.mp4; trim source first0frames and keep198frames. Preserve normal speed and complete two-frame pairs.
Narrator: “Our ancestors could keep embers glowing by feeding them wood. Making fire themselves was a different skill.”

Last frame / cut: trim the unnecessary tail after the main action and spoken turn. Continue the same held action state; no new stills or poses.
